chunks: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to me, from Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī, who said:

I heard Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying: Indeed Allah created us from the highest ʿIlliyyīn, and He created the hearts of our Shiʿah from that from which He created us, and He created their bodies from below that. So their hearts incline toward us because they were created from that from which we were created.
Then he recited this verse: “Nay! Indeed the record of the righteous is surely in ʿIlliyyīn. And what will make you know what ʿIlliyyūn is? A written book, witnessed by those brought near.”

And He created our enemy from Sijjīn, and He created the hearts of their adherents from that from which He created them, and their bodies from below that. So their hearts incline toward them because they were created from that from which they were created.
Then he recited this verse: “Nay! Indeed the record of the wicked is surely in Sijjīn. And what will make you know what Sijjīn is? A written book.”

key_terms.الْأَبْرَارِ: the righteous, whose record is in ʿIlliyyīn
key_terms.الْمُقَرَّبُونَ: those brought near to Allah, who witness the written record
key_terms.تَهْوِي: inclines, yearns, or is drawn emotionally and spiritually toward
key_terms.سِجِّينٍ: the constricted register or realm associated here with the wicked and the enemies
key_terms.شِيعَتِنَا: our Shiʿah; the devoted followers of the Imams
key_terms.عِلِّيِّينَ: the highest exalted register or realm associated here with the origin of the righteous and the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the spiritual bond between the Imams and their Shiʿah through ʿIlliyyīn and Sijjīn?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a theological account of the creation of the Ahl al-Bayt and the inner affinity of their Shiʿah, linking spiritual inclination to shared origin. It also contrasts this with the origin of their enemies and connects both realities to the Qur’anic categories of ʿIlliyyīn and Sijjīn.
